post_title: What will be the highest significant wave height at NDBC buoy 46026 (18 NM west of San Francisco) on November 26, 2026 (UTC)?

question.title: What will be the highest significant wave height at NDBC buoy 46026 (18 NM west of San Francisco) on November 26, 2026 (UTC)?
question.description:
NDBC station 46026 ("SAN FRANCISCO – 18NM West of San Francisco, CA") is a 3-meter foam buoy (SCOOP payload) moored at 37.750°N, 122.838°W in about 53 m of water on the continental shelf west of the Golden Gate. It reports roughly every 10 minutes, and its significant wave height (WVHT) is defined by NDBC as the average height of the highest one-third of waves during a 20-minute sampling period, reported in meters to one decimal place (see https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/measdes.shtml and the live station page https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/station_page.php?station=46026). The realtime standard meteorological file used for resolution holds roughly 45 days of 10-minute records, so November 26 data will be present on November 27.

Status as of November 13, 2026: the buoy was reading about 3.8 m (12.5 ft) of significant wave height with a 3.1 m swell at 13.8 s, in south winds of ~23 kt gusting 33 kt. A large long-period northwest swell from a distant hurricane-force low was hitting the California coast that weekend; NWS San Francisco forecast seas of roughly 25-30 ft offshore with breaking waves of 25-35 ft at exposed beaches, and High Surf Warnings were in effect along the Pacific coast from Humboldt and Mendocino down through the San Francisco Peninsula and Monterey Bay (https://www.weather.gov/mtr/).

Climatology: late November sits in the core of the eastern North Pacific storm season. Monthly-mean significant wave heights at offshore central California buoys run roughly 1.6-2.5 m in winter, with individual storms driving offshore seas to 5-7 m; on a typical late-November day the peak WVHT at 46026 falls somewhere around 2-3.5 m, calm days bottom out near 1.5 m, and major northwest groundswell events push daily maxima above 4-5 m. The value on any given day is set by the interplay of long-period northwest groundswell generated by Gulf of Alaska / North Pacific lows and locally generated wind sea from alongshore northwesterly winds, so guidance can be built from NWS coastal waters forecasts, NOAA WaveWatch III/GFS-Wave output, CDIP and surf-forecast products, and the buoy's own recent trend.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the highest value in the WVHT (significant wave height, in meters) column of the NDBC station 46026 realtime standard meteorological data file (https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/data/realtime2/46026.txt) among all rows whose timestamp (YY MM DD hh mm, UTC) falls on November 26, 2026, i.e. timestamps from 00:00 through 23:50 UTC on that date. For example, if the largest WVHT entry on that date reads 3.4, the question resolves to 3.4 m; if the largest reads 4.1, it resolves to 4.1 m. Rows in which WVHT is reported as "MM" are treated as missing and ignored. Only station 46026 (SAN FRANCISCO – 18NM West of San Francisco, CA, 37.750 N 122.838 W) is used, and no smoothing, averaging, or unit conversion is applied to the file's WVHT values.
question.fine_print: Resolution uses the realtime data file as it stands when the question resolves; later quality-controlled revisions of the same observations do not change the outcome. If the buoy reports no valid WVHT value at all for November 26, 2026 (for example, a sensor or mooring outage), the question will be annulled. If the realtime file itself is inaccessible, the same NDBC 46026 WVHT observations as published on other NDBC pages or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used.
